newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA STOCKS END DOWN, HURT BY FUTURES TRADERS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA STOCKS END DOWN, HURT BY FUTURES TRADERS.

text.p: South African shares end firmly down as futures traders, mindful of the contract close-out on Friday, push the market down as they aim to settle positions.
* Golds tumble on drifting bullion price as market ignores external factors such as softer-than-expected U.S. CPI data.

* Market seen drifting down all week, worries over looming July 1 relaxation of exchange controls and weakening rand also capping any positive sentiment. Volumes healthy with 825 million rands worth of shares traded.
* The all-share index loses 79.4 points to 7,192.1 as the industrials index drops 49.7 points to 8,432.7. Golds off 28.4 points, or 2.5 percent, to 1,100.5.
* M-Cell loses 16 cents to 560 cents after results. Good results figures boost Ozz 80 cents up to 27.20 rand, but poor results hit Gallagher which drops 27 cents to 99 cents.

* Most trade centred in blue-chips with De Beers losing 25 cents to 165.50 rand in trade worth 44 million rand, Anglo's drops 650 cents to 271.25 rand in trade worth 42.9 million rand and Sasol which sheds 50 cents to 56.50 rand in trade worth 38 million rand.
Individual shares had a mixed day with 123 stocks advancing, against 235 falling. Thirty sunk to new lows while 21 hit new highs.

Among firms posting results industrial holding firm Ozz jumped 80 cents to 27.20 rand as the market greeted healthy year growth, but traders judged annual results more harshly from M-Cell, the celluar phone company.
M-Cell lost 16 cents to 560 cents and Gallagher, which also posted poor results, shed 27 cents to 99 cents.

Information technology investment firm Mustek Ltd rose on Tuesday after saying it was in talks on a possible deal. The firm rose to match its year high of 15.00 rand before dropping back to 14.70 rand, a gain of 30 cents on the day.
Dealers said there was some speculation the firm may be talking to investment group Baobab about a possible link-up with Voicematrix, the specialist voice processing firm.
Baobab recently bought 25.1 percent of Voicematrix.
The Baobab stock finished the day up 200 cents to 41.00 rand.

Dealers said most trade by value was centred in blue-chips with De Beers losing 25 cents to 165.50 rand in trade worth 44 million rand, Anglo's dropping 650 cents to 271.25 rand in trade worth 42.9 million rand and Sasol shedding 50 cents to 56.50 rand in trade worth 38 million rand.
Overall the market saw a healthy 825 million rands worth of shares exchanging hands.
Dealers said the market was expected to continue on its downward trend all week until the futures close-out date was firmly out of the way.
"It is going to slip further while the market is still vulnerable to futures manipulation," one dealer said.
Gold shares took a battering from the drifting bullion price, though trade was light as most players have stayed away from the bombed-out index.
Golds ended off 28.4 points, or 2.5 percent, at 1,100.5.
Among individual shares Vaal Reefs fell 775 cents to 254.75 rand and Kloof was unchanged at 28.10 rand.
Futures dealers said they were still likely to sell equities as close-out approached, but added that many positions were settled already.

June futures contracts also weakened as the day hobbled on with the all-share contract last at 6,385/95 from 6,527 settlement and the industrials contract at 7,940/47 from 8,102. The golds contracts was last at 755/65 from 787.
-- Paul Harris, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
